access_model.notes: SPI NOR Flash. Read: 0x03 + 3-byte addr. Write: 0x02 + 3-byte addr + data. Sector erase: 0x20 + 3-byte addr. Page program 256B max.

operation_flows.description: SPI read: cmd 0x03 + 3-byte address + read data
SPI page program: WREN -> cmd 0x02 + 3-byte addr + data -> wait BUSY

transaction.notes: Page program: cmd + 3-byte addr + up to 256 data bytes

raw_encoding.notes: Raw byte stream from SPI flash. Addresses are 3-byte big-endian.

bitfields.name: BUSY
bitfields.description: Set during program/erase/write operations; clears when ready.

bitfields.name: WEL
bitfields.description: Write Enable Latch; set by Write Enable and cleared after write/erase operations.

bitfields.name: SEC
bitfields.description: Sector/block protect selector; 4KB sectors when set.

bitfields.name: SRP
bitfields.description: Status register protection bit; writable/lock behavior depends on SRL/SRP mode.

bitfields.name: SRL
bitfields.description: Status Register Protect Lock; can enforce power-supply lock-down or OTP mode.

bitfields.name: QE
bitfields.description: Quad Enable; enables Quad SPI and remaps /WP to IO2 and /HOLD to IO3 when set.

bitfields.name: LB3-1
bitfields.description: Security register lock bits; OTP protect security registers.

bitfields.name: CMP
bitfields.description: Complement protect bit; reverses selected protection region.

bitfields.name: WPS
bitfields.description: Selects status-register protection scheme versus individual block locks.

init_sequence.notes: After power-up, /CS must transition from high to low before a new instruction will be accepted.
Wait tPUW before issuing any write instruction after power-up.
If using Quad SPI, ensure QE=1 before quad read/program commands; default QE depends on ordering option.
For software reset, issue 66h then 99h in sequence; any other command between them cancels reset enable.

read_sequence.notes: For fast read variants, add the opcode-specific dummy clocks and use the appropriate data pins/IO width.

conversion_formulae.name: memory_bytes_passthrough
conversion_formulae.formula: Raw payload bytes are returned unchanged; no numeric conversion is applied.

conversion_formulae.name: jedec_device_id_passthrough
conversion_formulae.formula: JEDEC manufacturer/device ID bytes are returned as raw identity values.

conversion_formulae.name: status_register_bits_passthrough
conversion_formulae.formula: Status-register bits are consumed as control/status flags, not converted to a physical unit.

error_conditions.condition: Read Status Register or Read Data issued while BUSY=1 may return status only or be ignored depending on opcode; driver must poll BUSY before expecting array/data completion.
error_conditions.detection: BUSY bit in SR1 remains set after program/erase/write command or read opcode returns no progress within the operation timeout.
error_conditions.driver_action: poll until ready; if timeout expires, abort transaction and report -ETIMEDOUT

error_conditions.condition: Protected region targeted by Page Program, Erase, or Security Register write is ignored by the device.
error_conditions.detection: Write completes with BUSY behavior but target remains unchanged; protection bits/lock bits indicate coverage.

error_conditions.condition: WEL is not set before a write/erase/status/security operation.
error_conditions.detection: SR1.WEL=0 before issuing protected write opcode.

error_conditions.driver_action: fall back to standard SPI if supported, otherwise return -EOPNOTSUPP

error_conditions.condition: Reset sequence interrupted by any command other than 99h after 66h.
error_conditions.detection: Enable Reset state is canceled by intervening instruction.
error_conditions.driver_action: restart reset sequence from 66h; if unexpected state persists, reinitialize

error_conditions.condition: Release Power-down / Device ID while an erase/program/write cycle is active is ignored.
error_conditions.driver_action: retry after BUSY clears or report busy state to caller

power_states.name: standby
power_states.description: Normal operation after power-up; standby current applies when /CS is high and no internal cycle is running.

power_states.name: active
power_states.description: Device selected with /CS low; instructions can be written and data read.

power_states.name: power_down
power_states.description: Deep power-down entered by B9h; only ABh is recognized until released.

power_states.name: reset_state
power_states.description: After software or hardware reset, device returns to power-on state and volatile settings are lost.

requires_human: Confirm whether board policy prefers 9Fh JEDEC ID or 90h manufacturer/device ID as the canonical probe path; both are documented.
Confirm package/ordering-option-dependent QE default and whether the target part number is IM/JM or IQ/JQ so quad-mode initialization can be fixed correctly.
Confirm whether the target package has a dedicated /RESET pin; the excerpt notes package-dependent availability, and the target device family includes both hardware-reset and software-reset variants.
Confirm exact mapping of status-register S-bits to byte layout for any driver that needs bitwise writes; the excerpt uses S0..S23 notation and also 01h/31h/11h legacy behavior.
Confirm whether the device policy should use individual block/sector locks (WPS=1) or CMP/TB/BP protection (WPS=0) as the default write-protection scheme.
The excerpt says three security registers, while one sentence mentions 'four security registers'; use the three-register interpretation unless the full datasheet or system requirement says otherwise.
